alt: A formal dining room with a sculptural stone table and travertine sideboard beneath a two-storey steel window, shown in six bold material schemes—walls in oxblood, forest green, navy, charcoal, aubergine and teal, paired with contrasting pale and warm joinery, flooring, and hardware.
text:
when walls commit, everything else does too.

same dining room in six bold shifts—oxblood to teal. the stone reads differently. the wood finds new contrast. the metal catches light you didn't know was there. it's not about trend. it's about what becomes visible.

#formaldining #boldwalls #materialhierarchy #colourcontrast #spacedesign

provenance.base_prompt: A formal dining room with a sculptural stone table set against the long wall beneath a two-storey steel-framed window dividing at mid-height with a horizontal beam supporting a glass walkway—a passage crossing the upper glazing that establishes the room's dramatic scale. Open moorland visible beyond under shifting sky. To the right, a sculptural travertine sideboard with softly rounded forms topped with white-glazed stacked plates and a sculptural brass vessel. Left wall: recessed shelving built into plaster holds leather-bound books, white ceramics, a trailing green plant, and pale sculptural objects. A moulded-plaster pendant lamp centered above the table, organic and rounded. Flooring runs in wide boards. Textured linen window treatments frame the glazing. A travertine plinth table in the middle distance, circular and weighted, anchors layered objects and books. Summer light falls strong and direct, read primarily in reflected brightness across the floor, creating sharp contrast between deep shadow and high illumination across the room's depth
